incidents.name: Rocketcyber - eu.rocketcyber.com temporarily inaccessible

incident_updates.body:
` `**Public RCA: RocketCyber EU Production Service Interruption** 

**Incident Summary** 

On September 10, 2026, RocketCyber customers hosted in the EU region experienced service disruptions that prevented access to the RocketCyber console and caused intermittent failures in related platform services. The incident resulted in users receiving error messages when attempting to access the platform. Service was fully restored shortly after the event.  

We recognize the impact this disruption had on our partners and customers and apologize for the inconvenience. 

 

**Impact** 

**Affected Service:** RocketCyber EU Production Environment` ` **Impact Type:** Service Interruption` ` **Affected Users:** Customers utilizing the EU-hosted RocketCyber platform` ` **Duration:** Approximately 33 minutes for the primary console service disruption, with some dependent services recovering shortly thereafter.  

During the incident: 

* Users were unable to reliably access the RocketCyber console. 

* Some backend services experienced failures when processing requests. 

* Customers encountered server error messages while attempting to use the platform.  

 

**Timeline \(UTC\)** 

Timeline derived from the incident review.  

 

**Root Cause** 

The incident was caused by abnormal growth of certain database logging tables. Over time, these tables expanded significantly and exceeded operational thresholds. As the database attempted to protect itself and maintain data integrity, write operations became restricted and intensive maintenance processes consumed available database resources.  

This resource contention affected several dependent services, resulting in widespread application errors. As those services became unavailable, request traffic shifted to other platform components, creating additional load that ultimately impacted console availability.  

No customer data was lost or compromised during this event. The issue was related to system capacity and database maintenance processes rather than a security incident.  

 

**Resolution** 

The platform recovered as database maintenance activities completed and resource utilization returned to normal operating levels. Following service restoration, engineering teams continued monitoring platform health and performed additional analysis to validate system stability.  

 

**Preventive Actions** 

To reduce the likelihood of similar incidents, RocketCyber has implemented and is pursuing the following improvements: 

1. Reduced unnecessary logging activity that contributed to excessive database table growth.  

1. Reviewing and enhancing database growth monitoring and alerting to provide earlier visibility into capacity-related risks.  

1. Evaluating additional traffic management and rate-limiting mechanisms to help prevent cascading impacts during service degradation events.  

1. Developing operational guidance and runbooks to improve response efficiency for similar database-related incidents.  

 

**Current Status** 

All RocketCyber services are operating normally. Engineering teams have implemented immediate corrective measures and continue to strengthen monitoring and resilience controls to prevent recurrence.  

We appreciate your patience and understanding while this issue was being addressed.
This incident has been resolved.

The Kaseya R&D Team responded to alerts related to the eu.rocketcyber.com site.

The incident lasted for about 30 minutes during which Rocketcyber customers hosted in the EU region were not able to access the product.

The issue is now resolved, and we are currently monitoring the health of the service.

incidents.name: Datto EDR — Elevated Alert Volume — "Possible Shim Database Persistence via sdbinst.exe"

incident_updates.body:
**Datto EDR - Mass Detection on Windows Behavior – 2026-08-27** 

**Summary** 

Between **2026-08-27 08:00 UTC** and **2026-08-27 16:00 UTC**, Datto EDR customers experienced an elevated volume of detections generated by the **Possible Shim Database Persistence via sdbinst.exe** detection rule. The increase in alerts created additional operational overhead for customers and analysts reviewing alerts. No service outage occurred, and endpoint protection functionality remained operational throughout the event. The issue was resolved after the detection rule was updated to account for a newly observed legitimate Windows operating system behavior.  

**Root Cause** 

A legitimate Microsoft Windows behavior involving **sdbinst.exe** and the file path **C:\\Windows\\appcompat\\cloudsdb\\apppatch.sdb** was not covered by the existing exclusions within a Datto EDR detection rule. A change in Microsoft's behavior matched the criteria of the rule **Possible Shim Database Persistence via sdbinst.exe**, resulting in a higher-than-expected volume of detections. The rule logic was updated to properly account for the newly observed behavior and eliminate the unintended detections.  

**Incident Timeline** 

* **Identified:** 2026-08-27 08:00 UTC \(customer reports and alert volume increase identified\)  

* **Public Notification:** 2026-08-27 11:00 UTC \(incident escalated to Product and Detection Engineering teams and communications initiated\)  

* **Resolved:** 2026-08-27 16:00 UTC \(updated rule deployed and alert volume returned to expected levels\)  

**Preventative Measures** 

To reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents in the future, we are implementing the following improvements: 

**Enhancements to Monitoring and Alerting** 

* Implement monitoring and baselining for individual detection rules to identify abnormal spikes in alert volume more rapidly. 

* Develop internal metrics that provide visibility into detection trends and anomalous rule behavior before large-scale customer impact occurs.  

**Enhancements to Incident Management and Response** 

* Improve escalation workflows for significant detection-volume increases to ensure appropriate engineering resources are engaged as quickly as possible. 

* Continue refining response procedures for detection-rule tuning and validation when unexpected platform or operating system behavior changes are observed.  

**Detection Content Improvements** 

* Enhance detection engineering review processes to account for evolving operating system behaviors and newly introduced legitimate execution patterns. 

* Expand validation and exclusion testing for detection rules where operating system updates may introduce behavior changes that resemble suspicious activity.  

 

**Customer Impact** 

* Product Affected: **Datto EDR** 

* Impact Type: **Increased detection volume / mass alerts** 

* Service Availability: **No outage** 

* Security Protection Status: **Protection remained active and operational** 

* Customer Impact: Customers experienced increased alert volume requiring additional review and operational effort.  

This incident has been fully resolved, and Datto EDR continues to operate normally.
This incident has been resolved.

Microsoft's Program Compatibility Assistant (PCA) uses sdbinst.exe to manage application compatibility databases as part of routine Windows maintenance. The August Windows update introduced known gaming compatibility issues, and Microsoft's remediation of those issues triggered sdbinst.exe activity across affected endpoints simultaneously — matching the spike pattern we observed.

The affected rule has been updated as of 9:15 AM EST and pushed to all tenants. Alert volumes should return to expected levels. 

If you disabled the rule as a temporary measure, it is safe to re-enable it under Policies → Detections → "Possible Shim Database Persistence via sdbinst.exe".

We're seeing a spike in alerts for this rule caused by a recent change in Microsoft's default behavior. This is not indicative of active threats. A rule update is expected today.

In the meantime, you can temporarily disable the rule under Policies → Detections → "Possible Shim Database Persistence via sdbinst.exe" to reduce noise until the fix is deployed.

Should you need any additional questions or require assistance, please contact our support team at https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb#/contact

incidents.name: Error 500 in Datto Partner Portal for Backup & RMM Products.

incident_updates.body:
**Datto Partner Portal - Login Errors Affecting Partner Portal Users – 2026-09-02** 

**Summary:** Between **2026-09-02 06:30 AM UTC** and **2026-09-02 07:54 AM UTC**, **Datto Partner Portal** customers received HTTP 500 errors during authentication when logging into the Datto Partner Portal. 

  

**Root Cause:**  

A subset of users experienced login-related service disruptions resulting from storage capacity constraints within the production environment. As available storage resources became exhausted, authentication services were unable to process requests reliably, leading to an increase in login failures and degraded access to the platform. The issue was isolated to the affected production infrastructure, and remediation efforts were initiated to restore service stability and prevent recurrence. 

**Incident Timeline:**  

* Identified: **2026-09-02 06:30 AM UTC**  

* Public Notification: **2026-09-02 07:00 AM UTC**  

* Resolved: **2026-09-02 07:54 AM UTC** 

  

**Preventative Measures:** To reduce the likelihood and impact of similar incidents in the future, we are taking the following steps.   

* Modernize production storage capacity to align with current operational demands. Increase available storage resources and implement dedicated allocation for log retention to prevent routine growth from impacting service availability and overall system stability. 

* Strengthen operational monitoring through proactive capacity and service performance alerting.
This incident has been resolved.
We are continuing to monitor for any further issues.

We are pleased to inform you that the recent service incident experienced by our BCDR AND DRMM partners where users experienced difficulties logging into the Datto Partner Portal has now been successfully resolved. We understand the impact that such problems can have on your business operations, and we sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused during this time.

Our team has been diligently working to identify the root cause of the problem. Our goal is to not only address the immediate concern but also to minimize the risk of similar incidents in the future. By analyzing the underlying factors, we aim to enhance our systems and processes, ensuring a more robust and reliable experience for all our partners. 

Thank you for your patience and understanding. We remain committed to delivering exceptional service and continuous improvement.

incidents.name: Datto RMM / Datto EDR / Datto AV – Integration – Datto RMM Reporting Datto EDR and Datto AV Products as Not Detected

incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved.
A fix has been implemented and we are monitoring the results.

We have identified an issue affecting status reporting between Datto EDR, Datto AV, and Datto RMM. As a result, some devices may incorrectly generate alerts in Datto RMM indicating that Datto EDR requires attention or that Datto AV is not installed.

Our investigation has confirmed that Datto EDR and Datto AV remain installed and functioning properly on affected endpoints. Endpoint protection services continue to operate as expected. The issue is limited to the status information being reported and displayed within Datto RMM and does not indicate a loss of protection or a failure of the Datto EDR or Datto AV products.

Engineering teams have identified the underlying cause and are actively working on a resolution. We will continue to provide updates as additional information becomes available.

If you have questions or require assistance, please contact our support team at https://helpdesk.kaseya.com/hc/en-gb#/contact
